hindi: श्रीगणेश को नमस्कार।
english: Salutation to the revered Gaṇeśa.
notes: The leading '||' is a printed mark, kept as a token.

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम वमनकल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Vamana-kalpa (the formulations for emesis).

hindi: ऐसा आत्रेय आदि महर्षियों ने कहा।
english: Thus indeed said Ātreya and the other great sages.
notes: Ātreya is taken as a name; ha sma āhuḥ is a narrative formula ("indeed said").

words.gloss: fruits of madana (emetic nut, Randia spinosa; standard), jīmūtaka (Luffa echinata, bandal; probable), ikṣvāku (a bitter bottle-gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; disputed, and the reading is conjectural here), kukkṛtikā (unidentified), śātakī (unidentified) and kuṭaja (kurchi, Holarrhena pubescens; standard) (drug names)

hindi: वमन के द्रव्यों में मदन यानी मैनफल, जीमूतक, इक्ष्वाकु, कुक्कृतिका, शातकी और कुटज यानी कुड़ा के फल श्रेष्ठ हैं।
english: Among the substances for emesis, the fruits of madana (emetic nut), jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, kukkṛtikā, śātakī and kuṭaja (kurchi) are the best.

text_flags.why: 'kakṣvevāku' looks like a damaged 'ikṣvāku' (jīmūtaka+ikṣvāku); 'kukkṛtikā' and 'śātakī' are also doubtful (possibly kṛtavedhana / śyātakī in other books); not verified

notes: Drug names kept as names; the identifications are in the word gloss (owner policy 2026-10-17); only madana and kuṭaja are firm, the rest are tagged probable, disputed or unidentified. The long compound is damaged in the scan: the reading 'ikṣvāku' is a guess, the others kept as printed.

words.gloss: madana fruit (emetic nut; plant identified in unit 4)

hindi: उनमें भी मदनफल यानी मैनफल।
english: Among these too, the madana (emetic nut) fruit.
notes: Elliptical: no predicate in this unit (the sense of 'best' carries over from the previous unit); translated as printed.

words.gloss: by the sway of doṣa, what is vitiated (dūṣya), etc.

hindi: और इनमें तथा इन कल्पनाओं में प्राधान्य दोष, दूष्य आदि के वश से होता है।
english: And the precedence among these, and among these preparations, is according to doṣa, dūṣya (what is vitiated) and the like.
notes: 'eṣām etatkalpanānām' is taken as 'of these (drugs) and of these preparations'. Verb 'is' supplied.

words.gloss: from the very many differences of state

hindi: और दोष आदि की ही अत्यन्त बहुत अवस्थाओं के भेद से वमन आदि में कल्पों, व्यापदों और साधनों की जो असंख्यता है।
english: And because of the very many different states of doṣa and the rest, the formulations, mishaps and means in emesis and the like are innumerable.

text_flags.why: 'kalyāna' does not fit; 'kalpa' (formulations) is the sense and matches the chapter's theme
u+a would normally become 'va' (bahv-avasthā); possible misprint

notes: 'yad asaṃkhyeyatvam' is rendered as a statement ('...are innumerable'); the sentence continues in the next unit with 'ataḥ' (therefore).
lines_deva: दोषादीनामेव चातिबहुवस्थाभेदाद्वमनादिषु कल्यानां व्यापदां साधनानां च यदसंख्येयत्वं
lines_iast: doṣādīnāmeva cātibahuvasthābhedādvamanādiṣu kalyānāṃ vyāpadāṃ sādhanānāṃ ca yadasaṃkhyeyatvaṃ

words.gloss: for the purpose of showing the path of variations

hindi: इसलिए बुद्धिमानों को विकल्प के मार्ग का दर्शन कराने के लिए केवल उदाहरण के रूप में कल्पसिद्धिस्थान का उपदेश किया जाएगा।
english: Therefore, in order to show the intelligent the path of variations, the Kalpasiddhi section is taught as a mere example.
notes: 'mātra' taken as 'merely'. 'kalpasiddhisthāna' is the name of the section (Kalpa and Siddhi).

words.gram: loc. sg. (n. with ahani; m. if also with muhūrte)

words.gloss: madana fruits (emetic nut; plant identified in unit 4)

hindi: फिर वसन्त और ग्रीष्म के बीच, शुभ दिन और शुभ मुहूर्त में, न बहुत हरे और न बहुत पीले मदन यानी मैनफल के फलों को ग्रहण करे।
english: Then, in the interval between spring and summer, on an auspicious day and at an auspicious moment, one should take madana (emetic nut) fruits that are neither very green nor very pale.
notes: 'muhūrtte' is a variant spelling of muhūrte. 'harita-pāṇḍu' read as 'green and pale-yellow'; as a single compound it could mean 'green-pale'. praśaste may qualify only ahani, or both ahani and muhūrte; both translations take it with both.
lines_deva: अथ वसन्तग्रीष्मयोरन्तरे प्रशस्तेऽहनि मुहूर्त्ते च नातिहरितपांडूनि मदनफलान्याददीत
lines_iast: atha vasantagrīṣmayorantare praśaste'hani muhūrtte ca nātiharitapāṃḍūni madanaphalānyādadīta

words.gloss: in a bundle (mūḍaka) of kuśa grass (Desmostachya bipinnata; standard)

in a heap of any one of: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard), husk (busa), māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo; standard), śāli (winter rice, Oryza sativa; standard), vrīhi (rice, Oryza sativa, the ordinary rice grain; standard), kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard), mudga (green gram, Vigna radiata; standard)

hindi: उन्हें पोंछकर, कुश के मूढक में बाँधकर, गोबर से लीपकर, यव यानी जौ, बुस, माष यानी उड़द, शालि यानी अगहनी धान, व्रीहि यानी धान, कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी या मुद्ग यानी मूँग में से किसी एक की राशि में आठ रात रखे हुए को निकालकर धूप में सुखाए।
english: Having wiped them, tied them in a bundle of kuśa grass and smeared it with cow-dung, and (having kept them) for eight nights in a heap of any one of yava (barley), husk (busa), māṣa (black gram), śāli (winter rice), vrīhi (rice), kulattha (horse gram) or mudga (green gram), one should take them out and dry them in the sun.

text_flags.why: absolutive of √bandh normally has the doubled dh; possible misprint

notes: 'mūḍaka' is taken as 'bundle' (compare Marathi mūḍh); uncertain. 'busa' read as husk/chaff, 'yava-busa' could also be read as 'barley-husk'. Grain names are kept as names. The packet (smeared with cow-dung) is taken as the thing kept in the heap; the Sanskrit does not state this.
lines_deva: तानि प्रमृज्य कुशमूडके बध्वा गोमयेनालिप्य यवबुसमाषशालिव्रीहिकुलत्थमुद्गान्यतमराशावष्टरात्रमुषितान्युद्धृत्यातपे शोषयेत्
lines_iast: tāni pramṛjya kuśamūḍake badhvā gomayenālipya yavabusamāṣaśālivrīhikulatthamudgānyatamarāśāvaṣṭarātramuṣitānyuddhṛtyātape śoṣayet

words.gloss: pippalī (drug name; the bare word usually means long pepper, Piper longum, standard for that word; in this madana chapter 'phalapippalī' probably means the dried madana fruit pieces, probable, see notes)
rubbed with curd, ghee, honey and palala

hindi: भली-भाँति सूखे हुओं में से पिप्पलियों को निकालकर, दही, घी, शहद और पलल में मसली हुई उन्हें फिर सुखाकर, नए और धूल-रहित कलश को गले तक भरकर, उसे अच्छी तरह सुरक्षित रखवाए।
english: From the well-dried ones, having taken out the pippalīs, rubbed with curd, ghee, honey and palala, and dried them again, one should fill a new, dust-free pot up to the neck and have it stored well guarded.
notes: 'pippalī' is not glossed beyond the name here (it is the thing drawn out of the dried fruits; the identity is not stated). 'palala' literally paste (also flesh/sesame paste in dictionaries); kept as a name. The pot is understood to be filled with the rubbed pippalīs. Identification: bare 'pippalī' is long pepper (Piper longum; standard). Here, in the chapter on madana, the 'pippalīs' drawn out of the dried fruits and called 'phalapippalī' in the next units are probably the dried madana fruit pieces themselves (the commentators' reading, as far as I recall; probable, not certain), so 'long pepper' is not put in the translation. 'palala' is ground sesame paste in some references (kept as the name palala).
lines_deva: सुशुष्काणां पिप्पलीरुद्धृत्य दधिघृतमधुपललविमृदिताः पुनः शोषयित्वा नवं कलशमरजस्कमाकंठं पूरयित्वा सुगुप्तं निधापयेत्
lines_iast: suśuṣkāṇāṃ pippalīruddhṛtya dadhighṛtamadhupalalavimṛditāḥ punaḥ śoṣayitvā navaṃ kalaśamarajaskamākaṃṭhaṃ pūrayitvā suguptaṃ nidhāpayet

words.gloss: of the fruit-pippalīs (here probably the dried madana fruit pieces, as in unit 11; probable)
a fist with the mouth inward (a handful)

in the decoction of any one of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; standard), kovidāra (orchid tree, Bauhinia variegata; standard), karbudāra (Bauhinia purpurea; probable), nīpa (kadamba, Neolamarckia cadamba; probable), vidula (cane, Calamus rotang, or a willow, Salix; disputed), bimbī (ivy gourd, Coccinia grandis; standard), śaṇapuṣpī (a Crotalaria species of the sunn-hemp type; disputed), sadāpuṣpī (possibly a name of arka, Calotropis gigantea; disputed), pratyakpuṣpī (prickly chaff-flower, Achyranthes aspera; standard) (drug names)
by the method stated in the Sūtra (section)

hindi: तब प्रयोग के समय उन फल-पिप्पलियों की भीतर की ओर मुँह वाली एक मुट्ठी, अथवा जितनी ठीक समझे, कूटकर यष्टीमधुक यानी मुलेठी, कोविदार यानी कचनार, कर्बुदार, नीप यानी कदम्ब, विदुल, बिम्बी यानी कुन्दरू, शणपुष्पी, सदापुष्पी या प्रत्यक्पुष्पी यानी चिरचिटा में से किसी एक के कषाय में, अथवा रात भर रखे, मसले और छाने हुए को सूत्रस्थान में कही विधि से पिलाए।
english: Then, at the time of use, one should coarsely crush a fist (with the mouth inward) of those fruit-pippalīs, or as much as one thinks fit, and, in the decoction of any one of yaṣṭīmadhuka (liquorice), kovidāra (orchid tree), karbudāra, nīpa (kadamba), vidula, bimbī (ivy gourd), śaṇapuṣpī, sadāpuṣpī or pratyakpuṣpī (prickly chaff-flower), or else kept for a night, rubbed and strained, have it drunk by the method stated in the Sūtra section.
notes: 'antarmukhamuṣṭim' (a fist with the mouth inward) is uncertain: it may be a handful measure; the printed sense is kept. The second 'vā' after 'kaṣāye' is ambiguous (alternative way of taking it); rendered as 'or else'. All names are drug names; identifications are in the word gloss (owner policy 2026-10-17). 'Sūtra' is taken as the Sūtrasthāna.
lines_deva: ततः प्रयोगकाले तासां फलपिप्पलीनामंतर्मुखमुष्टिं यावद्वा साधु मन्येत जर्जरीकृत्य यष्टीमधुककोविदारकर्बुदारनीपविदुलबिंबीशणपुष्पीसदापुष्पीप्रत्यक्पुष्प्यन्यतमकषाये वा रात्रिमुषितं विमृदितं पूतं सूत्रोक्तविधिना पाययेत्
lines_iast: tataḥ prayogakāle tāsāṃ phalapippalīnāmaṃtarmukhamuṣṭiṃ yāvadvā sādhu manyeta jarjarīkṛtya yaṣṭīmadhukakovidārakarbudāranīpavidulabiṃbīśaṇapuṣpīsadāpuṣpīpratyakpuṣpyanyatamakaṣāye vā rātrimuṣitaṃ vimṛditaṃ pūtaṃ sūtroktavidhinā pāyayet

words.gloss: in phlegm (kapha), fever, gulma (abdominal lump), pratiśyāya (coryza, running cold) and internal abscesses (antar-vidradhi)

hindi: कफ, ज्वर, गुल्म यानी पेट के भीतर की गाँठ, प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम और भीतरी विद्रधि यानी भीतरी फोड़े में विशेष रूप से, फिर पित्त के आने तक।
english: Especially in phlegm (śleṣma), fever, gulma (abdominal lump), pratiśyāya (coryza, common cold) and internal abscesses, again until Pitta comes.
notes: Continues the sentence of the previous unit. 'śleṣmajvara' could also be read as 'kapha-fever'; 'punar ā-pitta-gamanāt' is obscure ('repeatedly until pitta comes up'?); translated closely with a supplied verb in Hindi.

hindi: उससे भली प्रकार वमन होता है।
english: By that one vomits well.

words.gloss: powder of triphalā (three-fruit group: harītakī, Terminalia chebula; bibhītaka, Terminalia bellirica; āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica; standard) in three parts
with the decoction of kovidāra and the rest

strong kapha, praseka (flow, trickling; in clinical use excessive salivation), apaci (chain of glandular swellings, cervical lymphadenitis / scrofula; probable), arbuda (tumour, growth), granthi (nodular swelling, cyst), fever, udara (belly)
in loss of relish for food

hindi: अथवा अपने क्वाथ में भावित फल-पिप्पली का चूर्ण, तीन भाग त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला के चूर्ण के साथ, कोविदार आदि के क्वाथ से, प्रबल कफ, प्रसेक यानी मुँह में पानी भर आना, अपची यानी गण्डमाला, अर्बुद यानी ट्यूमर, ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ, ज्वर, उदर और अरुचि में पिए।
english: Or the powder of fruit-pippalī steeped in its own decoction, with triphalā (harītakī, bibhītaka and āmalakī: the three myrobalans) powder in three parts, one should drink with a decoction of kovidāra and the rest, in strong Kapha, praseka (excessive salivation), apaci (glandular swellings of the neck), arbuda (tumour), granthi (nodular swelling, cyst), fever, udara and arocaka (loss of relish for food).
notes: The printed line breaks the word 'jvarodarā rocakeṣu': the space splits 'udara-arocakeṣu' in the middle of a sandhi (a+a=ā). The first token is given 'udara-' and the second 'arocakeṣu'. 'balavat' may qualify only 'kapha' or all the conditions. 'tribhāga' could also mean 'a third part'. Modern equivalents: udara in a list of diseases usually means udara roga (disease of the belly, such as abdominal enlargement); the translation keeps 'belly' as decided. Triphalā members are standard (harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalakī). The 'kovidāra and the rest' group (kovidārādi) is not enumerated here.
lines_deva: फलपिप्पलीचूर्णं वा स्वक्वाथभावितं त्रिभागत्विफलाचूर्णं कोविदारादिनिर्यूहेण बलवत्कफप्रसेकापच्यर्बुदग्रंथिज्वरोदरा रोचकेषु पिबेत्
lines_iast: phalapippalīcūrṇaṃ vā svakvāthabhāvitaṃ tribhāgatviphalācūrṇaṃ kovidārādiniryūheṇa balavatkaphaprasekāpacyarbudagraṃthijvarodarā rocakeṣu pibet

words.gloss: powder of the kernel of the madana fruit
with the decoction of jīmūtaka and the rest
gone to the seat of kapha

hindi: अथवा मदनफल यानी मैनफल की मज्जा का चूर्ण जीमूतक आदि के क्वाथ से, जब पित्त कफ के स्थान में गया हो।
english: Or the powder of the kernel of the madana (emetic nut) fruit, with a decoction of jīmūtaka and the rest, when Pitta has gone to the seat of Kapha.
notes: 'majjā' taken as the inner kernel (literally marrow). No verb in the unit; the sentence is elliptical.

words.gloss: cooked with the kernel of the madana fruit
in raktapitta (blood-pitta; a bleeding disorder, bleeding from the upper or lower passages)

hindi: अथवा मदनफल यानी मैनफल की मज्जा से सिद्ध किया दूध, या उसी में यवागू, निचले भाग में रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव के रोग में और हृदय की जलन में।
english: Or milk cooked with the kernel of the madana (emetic nut) fruit, or a gruel (yavāgū) in that, in raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) in the lower part and in burning of the heart (heartburn).
notes: 'adhobhāge' may mean 'in the lower part (of the body)' going with raktapitta, or 'in the lower portion (of the milk/preparation)'; the former is rendered. 'majja' is read as a variant of 'majjā'.
lines_deva: मदनफलमज्जसिद्धं वा पयस्तस्मिन्वा यवागूमधोभागे रक्तपित्ते हृद्दाहे च
lines_iast: madanaphalamajjasiddhaṃ vā payastasminvā yavāgūmadhobhāge raktapitte hṛddāhe ca

words.gloss: santānikā (the film/skin that forms on milk)
when the chest, throat and heart

hindi: अथवा उस ठंडे दूध की संतानिका यानी मलाई की एक अञ्जलि, जब पित्त कुपित हो और छाती, कंठ तथा हृदय पतले कफ से लिप्त हों।
english: Or a palmful of the santānikā (skin, milk-cream) of that cold milk, when Pitta is aggravated and the chest, throat and heart are smeared with thin Kapha.
notes: 'santānikā' is taken as the film that forms on milk. 'uraḥkaṇṭhahṛdaye' is read as a dvandva in the locative, agreeing with 'upādigdhe'.
lines_deva: तस्य वा पयसः शीतस्य संतानिकांऽजलिं पित्ते प्रकुपिते उरःकंठहृदये च तनुकफोपादिग्धे
lines_iast: tasya vā payasaḥ śītasya saṃtānikāṃ'jaliṃ pitte prakupite uraḥkaṃṭhahṛdaye ca tanukaphopādigdhe

words.gloss: in kapha, vomiting (chardi), praseka (flow, trickling; in clinical use excessive salivation) and tamaka (a breathing disorder, bronchial asthma; if the damaged reading 'tamaka' is right)

hindi: अथवा उससे उत्पन्न दही, या दही का ऊपरी भाग, कफ, छर्दि, प्रसेक यानी मुँह में पानी भर आना और तमक यानी दमे का एक भेद में।
english: Or the curd born of that, or the upper part of the curd (dadhyuttara), in Kapha, vomiting, praseka (excessive salivation) and tamaka (a form of breathlessness, asthma).

text_flags.why: 'tanmaka' is probably 'tamaka' (a named condition); possible misprint

notes: 'dadhyuttara' rendered literally as the upper part of curd; the sense is not certain. 'tamaka' is a condition name, kept as a name.
lines_deva: तज्जं वा दधि दध्युत्तरं वा कफच्छर्दिप्रसेकतन्मकेषु
lines_iast: tajjaṃ vā dadhi dadhyuttaraṃ vā kaphacchardiprasekatanmakeṣu

words.gloss: with a decoction of the six beginning with phala
mixed with the powder of the six phalas
when the body is drying up

hindi: अथवा उस दूध से उत्पन्न नवनीत यानी मक्खन, फलादि छह के क्वाथ से और छह फलों के चूर्ण से मिलाकर सिद्ध किया हुआ, जब अग्नि यानी पाचन की अग्नि कफ से दबी हो और शरीर सूख रहा हो।
english: Or the fresh butter produced from that milk, cooked with a decoction of the six beginning with phala and mixed with the powder of the six phalas, when the fire (agni, the digestive fire) is overcome by Kapha and the body is drying up.
notes: 'phalādiṣaṭ' and 'phalaṣaṭ' (the six phalas) are not enumerated in this unit.

hindi: अथवा फल-पिप्पली के स्वरस और कषाय से पीड़ित किए हुए, तिल और शालि यानी अगहनी धान के चावल के पिसे हुए आटों से, उसी के कषाय से मिले हुए, या सुरसा आदि द्रव्यों में से किसी एक के क्वाथ से मिले हुए, शष्कुली, अपूप अथवा अन्य भक्ष्य बनाकर खाए।
english: Or, with ground tila (sesame) and śāli (winter rice) grain pressed with the juice and decoction of fruit-pippalī and mixed with its decoction, or mixed with the decoction of any one of the substances beginning with surasā, one should prepare śaṣkulī cakes, apūpa cakes or another food, and eat it.
notes: 'śaṣkulī' and 'apūpa' are kinds of cakes. 'tila' is sesame in common usage; kept as the name.
lines_deva: फलपिप्पलीस्वरसकषायपरिपीडतैर्वा तिलशालितंडुलपिष्टैस्तत्कषायोपसृष्टैः सुरसादिद्रव्यान्यतमनिर्यूहोपसृष्टैर्वा शष्कुलीरपूपानन्यं वा भक्ष्यं साधयित्वा भक्षयेत्

english: Or the juice of the fruit-pippalīs, as heard in the bhallātaka (marking nut) procedure, having cooked it until it coats the ladle, one should have it licked.
notes: 'bhallātakavidhi' refers to a procedure for bhallātaka described elsewhere; not imported here.

hindi: अथवा उस लेह को अन्न और पान में मिलाए।

hindi: अथवा फल की मज्जा का क्वाथ, वत्सक यानी कुटज आदि के प्रक्षेप सहित, निम्ब यानी नीम या अर्क यानी आक में से किसी एक के कषाय से मिला हुआ, संतर्पण से उत्पन्न सब कफ-रोगों को हरने वाला।
english: Or the decoction of the fruit kernel, with an addition of vatsaka (kuṭaja) and the rest, mixed with the decoction of either nimba (neem) or arka (swallow-wort), removing all Kapha ailments arising from satiation (saṃtarpaṇa).
notes: 'hara' (removing) is as printed: the text itself states this, it is not added by the draft. No verb in the unit; elliptical like the units before it.

words.gram: pres. part. upa-√ghrā, m. nom. sg.

words.gloss: one whose kapha and pitta are stirred by a fitting abundance of fragrance

hindi: अथवा फल आदि के क्वाथ से इक्कीस बार भली-भाँति भावित फल-पिप्पलियों को पुष्प के पराग के समान चूर्ण से चूर्णित करे। संध्या के समय सरोवर में बड़े कमल में रखकर रात भर रखे उसे प्रातः फिर चूर्ण मिलाकर निकाल ले। हरिद्रा यानी हल्दी, कृसरा यानी खिचड़ी, दूध या यवागू में से किसी एक को सेंधा नमक, गुड़ और फाणित यानी राब मिलाकर गले तक पीकर, सूँघता हुआ, सुकुमार, उचित गन्ध की सम्पदा से जिसके कफ और पित्त उभर आए हों और जो औषध से द्वेष रखता हो, वह इस प्रकार सुख से वमन करता है।
english: Or the fruit-pippalīs, well steeped twenty-one times in a decoction of phala and the rest, one should dust over with a powder like flower pollen; in the evening, in a lake, a large lotus; that kept for a night, and in the morning taken out and powdered again; having drunk up to the neck any one of haridrā (turmeric), kṛsarā (a rice-and-pulse dish, khichdi), milk or gruel, with rock salt, jaggery and phāṇita (thick cane-juice syrup) added, smelling, a delicate person, whose Kapha and Pitta are stirred by a fitting abundance of fragrance and who hates medicine, thus vomits easily.
notes: This unit is long and partly unclear. 'sarasi saroruhaṃ bṛhat sāyāhne tadrātrim uṣitam' is read as 'in the evening, (placed) in a large lotus in a lake, that kept for a night'; the verb is not in the text. The relation of the powder to the drink ('anyatamam ... pītavān') and the reading 'haridrā-kṛsarā' (one dish or two) are uncertain. 'samucitagandhasampadutkliṣṭakaphapitto' is read as one bahuvrīhi (stirred by a fitting abundance of fragrance); it could also be a list of separate qualities of the person. 'chardayati' is the printed present, rendered 'vomits'. The Hindi is a literal reading, not smoothed. Modern equivalents for haridrā and kṛsarā follow the printed split; if 'haridrākṛsarā' is one dish the turmeric identification would not apply (this unit stays low confidence).
lines_deva: फलपिप्पलीनां वा फलादिनिर्यूहेणैकविंशतिकृत्वः सुभावितानां कुसुमरजःसदृशेन चूर्णेनावचूर्णयेत् सरसि सरोरुहं बृहत सायान्हे तद्रात्रिमुषितं प्रभाते पुनरुपचूर्णितमुद्धृत्य हरिद्राक्रसराक्षीरयवागूनामन्यतमं सैंधवगुडफाणितोपेतमाकंठं पीतवानुपजिघ्रन् सुकुमारः समुचितगंधसंपदुत्क्लिष्टकफपित्तो भेषजद्वेषी च तथा सुखेन च्छर्दयति

hindi: इस प्रकार फल की विधि कही गई।

loc. pl. of an a-stem should be -eṣu; possible misprint

lines_deva: तत्र पुष्पेषु क्षीरं फलेषु पेयां लोमलोमवत्सु फलेषु शेषेषु संतानिकां निर्लोमसु दधि दध्युत्तरकं वा

words.gloss: in kapha, loss of relish (arocaka, anorexia), cough (kāsa), pāṇḍu disease (anaemia) and yakṣman (consumption, wasting disease; includes what is now called tuberculosis)

hindi: अथवा उसके कषाय से मिली हुई सुरा यानी अनाज की मदिरा को कफ, अरोचक यानी अरुचि, कास यानी खाँसी, पाण्डुरोग यानी रक्ताल्पता और यक्ष्मन् यानी क्षय रोग में प्रयोग करे।
english: Or one should use surā (grain liquor) mixed with its decoction in Kapha, arocaka (loss of relish for food), cough, pāṇḍu disease (anaemia) and yakṣman (consumption; includes what is now called tuberculosis).
